text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Pakistan can save $400 million by systematic management of petroleum product imports and plugging system losses of electricity which have mounted to $3.4 billion a year.
- President Farooq Leghari has promulgated a Central Depositories Ordinance, which will promote credibility and transparency and stop fictitious share trading.
- Pakistan Telecommunications Company Ltd (PTCL) has moved towards its privatisation.
- The Supreme Court will announce its judgement on former prime minister Benazir Bhutto's petition for restoration of her government.
- Former prime minister Moeen Qureshi has rushed to Pakistan amid a developing situation where many analysts believe he may again be asked to become the caretaker prime minister.
- The Council for Defence and National Security has discussed the prospect of its continuation beyond February 3 elections and reviewed the accountability process.

- Police in Punjab province have registered a case against Asif Ali Zardari, husband of Benazir Bhutto, former Punjab chief minister Arif Nakai and others in connection with the murder of a Jamaat-i-Islami activist at Mansoora in October.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Income Tax Commissioners have been asked to freeze the bank accounts of defaulters of wealth tax in order to speed up recoveries of arrears amounting to 1.2 billion rupees.

- The government has allowed import of basic raw material for pharmaceutical industry from India to rationalise the price structure of medicines and decided to privatise the remaining nine units of the state-run Ghee Corporation of Pakistan.
- The IMF has released the second tranche of $75 million (SDR 53.58 million) under the augmented Standby Arrangement.

- The Karachi Stock Exchange has urged the government to use competitive bidding in local and international markets to launch the $150 million issue of five-year notes exchangeable with shares of PTCL.
FINANCIAL POST
- The central bank has issued a series of policy orders to revamp the banking sector.
THE NEWS
- A Gallup Pakistan poll shows that Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League holds a clear lead over Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party.
THE FRONTIER POST
- Information Minister Irshad Haqqani said a transfer of power after the elections could be delayed "even by two months" to complete post-election scrutiny of winning candidates.
